questions.question: Define index fossil.
questions.solution_html:
• Define index fossil. / [CO1]
  • • A fossil used for dating and correlating the strata in which it is found. (1 Mark)
  • • Must have a wide geographic distribution and a short vertical (geological) time range. [1

questions.question: What does the term 'ancestral traits' mean ?
questions.solution_html:
• What does the term 'ancestral traits' mean? / [CO1]
  • • Characteristics inherited from a distant common ancestor that have remained unchanged
  • through a lineage. (1 Mark)
  • • Any Examples: Body hair in primates is an ancestral trait inherited from a mammalian
  • ancestor. (1 Mark)

• Define interambulacra. / [CO2]

questions.question: Examine the importance of palynology in petroleum exploration.
questions.solution_html:
• Examine the importance of palynology in petroleum exploration. / [CO3]
  • • Bio-stratigraphic correlation: Using pollen/spores to correlate layers across different wells. [3
  • Marks]
  • • Paleo-environmental reconstruction: Determining if the source rock was marine or
  • terrestrial. (2 Marks)
  • • Thermal Maturity: Analyzing the color of palynomorphs (Thermal Alteration Index) to see if
  • the organic matter reached the "oil window." (3 Marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain tracks, trails and borings.
questions.solution_html:
• Explain tracks, trails, and borings. / [CO1]
  • • Tracks: Individual footprints or impressions left by an organism's feet or appendages. [2
  • Marks]
  • • Trails: Continuous traces left by an organism crawling or dragging its body (e.g., worm trails).
  • (3 Marks)
  • • Borings: Holes or excavations made by organisms into hard substrates like shells, wood, or
  • rock. (3 Marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Classify gastropods based on shell characters.
questions.solution_html:
• Classify gastropods based on shell characters. / [CO2]
  • • Coiling: Dextral (right-handed) vs. Sinistral (left-handed) or planispiral vs. conispiral. [3
  • Marks]
  • • Aperture characteristics: Presence of a siphonal notch, peristome, or operculum. (2 Marks)
  • • Ornamentation: Ribs, spines, or growth lines on the whorls. (3 Marks)

questions.question: Evaluate the role of invertebrate fossils in paleogeographic reconstructions. Also discuss how fossil assemblages help in identifying past continental positions and marine connections.
questions.solution_html:
• Invertebrate fossils in paleogeographic reconstructions. / [CO4]
  • • Continental Positions: Using fossil distributions (e.g., Glossopteris or specific trilobites) to
  • prove former land connections (Gondwana). (4 Marks)
  • • Marine Connections: Identifying shared marine fauna between now-separated basins to
  • indicate ancient seaways or barriers. (4 Marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain conditions of fossilization. Add a note on body fossils. [8x3 = 24]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain conditions of fossilization and note on body fossils. / [CO1]
  • • Conditions: 1. Preservation of original soft part without alteration. 2. Preservation of original
  • hard part without alteration. 3. Preservation of altered hard parts. 4. Preservation of traces
  • or evidence of animal activities. (4 Marks)
  • • Body Fossils: Remains of the actual organism (shells, bones, teeth) preserved via
  • permineralization, replacement, or moulds/casts. (4 Marks)

questions.question: Describe the internal parts of a Cephalopod shell, focusing on siphuncle, septa, septal necks, connecting rings and chambers.
questions.solution_html:
• Internal parts of a Cephalopod shell. / [CO2]
  • • Septa & Chambers: Cross-walls (septa) that divide the shell into gas-filled buoyancy
  • chambers (camerae). (3 Marks)
  • • Siphuncle: A tube of living tissue extending through the septa to regulate buoyancy. [3
  • Marks]
  • • Septal Necks: Extensions of the septa that support the siphuncle at the point of entry. [3
  • Marks]
  • • Connecting Rings: Segments of the siphuncle between the septal necks. (3 Marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain Palaeontology definition, scope and applications. [12x1 = 12]
questions.solution_html:
• Palaeontology: Definition, scope, and applications. / [CO1]
  • • Definition: The study of ancient life through fossils. (2 Marks)
  • • Scope: Includes Palaeobotany, Palaeozoology, Micropalaeontology, and Ichnology. (4 Marks)
  • • Applications:
  • o Geological: Age determination, correlation, and stratigraphy. (3 Marks)
  • o Biological/Industrial: Understanding evolution, paleoclimate studies, and
  • exploration for fossil fuels (Coal/Oil). (3 Marks)
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026
